rv.q: It begins the first chapter of Charles Dickens’ David Copperfield , the chapter itself entitled “I Am Born, as outstanding a chapter heading as there is on any library shelf. Given all that, I’m happy to report that Jeffrey Scharf, who wrangled book, music, and lyrics for Copperfield!
It's the 19th-century literature musical I didn't know I needed.
Gabriel Barre does a very spirited job of direction and choreography.

This is a rich, heartwarming story of grievous loss and great resilience embodied in theatrically heightened but still recognizable characters, both devilish and angelic; it’s a tale and characters that, even in so greatly abbreviated a form, makes you care about them.
Despite its pacing problems, Copperfield! will likely delight Dickens fans and create some new ones, but it only partly fulfills its great expectations.
Still, nothing onstage at The Duke on 42nd Street convinces one that a David Copperfield musical is desirable or necessary.

Jeffrey Scharf’s Copperfield! honors the hardships of Dickens’ most personal novel while giving it a big, warm heart, with Bobby Conte and a tireless ensemble making the long road home worth every step.
The complicated story arrives with clarity by way of book, music and lyric writer Jeffrey Scharf and director Gabriel Barre.
On the contrary, the new Copperfield! is an energetic and melodious delight.
This is a highly recommended and ambitious, mostly delicious enterprise.
But admiration for ambition is not the same as emotional engagement.
As messy as it is entertaining, Copperfield! The New Musical feels staggeringly comprehensive, hilariously preposterous, and deeply moving all at once.

cn.t: This tuneful Dickens adaptation earns mostly positive reviews for its warmth and talented multi-tasking cast, though some critics find the sprawling novel remains resistant to musicalization despite Jeffrey Scharf's efforts.

vr.q: It's just a delightful night at the theater.
So, go check out Copperfield the new musical... well-told story, well-done. It just really well-done by everyone involved.
